title: Running-job conflict check is not atomic
reasoning: The route promises a 409 when a digest job is already running, but generate_digest first queries for an active processing row and only later inserts a new processing row. There is no unique active-job constraint or transactional lock shown on the digests table. Two concurrent POST /trigger requests can both observe no running job before either commits, causing both to start pipelines instead of one receiving 409.
recommendation: Move the active-job guard into an atomic database operation, for example a singleton lock table or transaction that serializes job creation, and keep a process-level async lock only as an optimization. Preserve stale-lock handling inside the same critical section.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked or discovered tests exercise concurrent POST /digests/trigger requests; existing tests found in this area cover downloads and unrelated podcast triggers.
suggestedRegressionTest: Use an async test client to issue two authenticated POST /api/digests/trigger requests concurrently with the pipeline held open, then assert exactly one response is 200 and the other is 409 and only one processing digest row exists.
minimumFixScope: Atomic job-start logic in app/worker/bindery.py plus a concurrent trigger regression test.
